findings.title: Cutting hard rock into a bounded place

findings.mechanism: The focus stone carrier at 89:5:6:1 meets the separate cutting, hard-rock, valley, and hollow nominations anchored at 89:8 and 89:9, so the question's possessor of hijr is placed beside resistance being opened, bounded, and made inhabitable.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive physical shape in the question's boundary language while keeping the ordinary reading of hijr as the quality of the discerning person recoverable.
findings.containment: This remains a qualified pericope-level contextual image. Valley, cutting, and water-holding hollow are not asserted as lexical definitions of hijr; the hollow/new-well facet is a trusted nominated source image without a separately verified focus occurrence or standalone water term.

findings.title: Monumental hardness and the inner limit
findings.claim: The pericope lets the possessor of hijr be seen as one whose inward restraint is tested by outward command of columns, measured construction, cut rock, and stakes.
findings.mechanism: The attributed HFT trace connects the focus oath, stone, and inward-restraint roles to the context's columns, measured making, rock-cutting, massive rock, stakes, transgression, corruption, and watchpoint; the later crossing and disorder reverse the external architecture into a test of inner boundary.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see why the question's disciplined intellect carries an inward boundary alongside its physical stone pressure: monumental capacity displays power, while the later verbs expose whether power becomes restraint.
findings.containment: This is an exploratory attributed contextual contrast, not a claim that the historical building vocabulary deliberately defines hijr. The unresolved HFT branches carry only their supplied roles, and reciprocal weak or no-value connection rows limit directness while leaving the anchored trace visible.

epistemic.reason: The trace gives exact pericope coordinates, attributed roles, a changed reading, and focus returns, but its reader identity is legacy_unbound and reconstructed; the antithesis is therefore kept exploratory.
